overview: This one-page Department of State filing index for decimal file 894C.515 identifies two consular despatches from Dairen to the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo concerning the planned prohibition of small Chinese silver coinage in the Kwantung Leased Territory. The first reports an announcement that the prohibition would begin in April 1936; the second concerns the ban after April 1, 1936, and notes enclosures comprising Imperial Ordinance No. 313 and Kwantung Bureau Ordinances Nos. 73 and 74.

people.name: Grummon
people.role: Consular officer associated with the Dairen despatches; exact title not stated

subfiles.title: List of papers on the prohibition of small Chinese silver coinage
subfiles.about: An index sheet records two Dairen consular despatches concerning the prohibition of small Chinese silver coins in the Kwantung Leased Territory beginning in April 1936.
subfiles.summary: The first entry describes a Dairen Consulate despatch forwarding an announcement that small Chinese silver coinage would be prohibited beginning in April 1936. The second lists a despatch about the prohibition of such coinage after April 1, 1936, accompanied by copies of Imperial Ordinance No. 313 and Kwantung Bureau Ordinances Nos. 73 and 74. Both despatches were addressed to the Embassy in Tokyo and are associated with Grummon.

interest: The sheet is useful as a compact guide to otherwise separate diplomatic records documenting Japanese monetary regulation in the Kwantung Leased Territory. Its references to specific imperial and bureau ordinances allow historians to connect U.S. consular reporting with the territory’s colonial legal framework. It also points to the attempted removal of small Chinese silver currency as part of a broader reordering of money and economic administration in the region.
